units.source: "把" moves the object before the verb when you're doing something specific TO it - "把...写下来" means "write [it] down".

units.source: Using 把 with a general, non-specific object - 把 requires the object to be something specific both speakers already have in mind.
units.translation: Usar 把 con un objeto general, no específico; 把 requiere que el objeto sea algo concreto que ambos hablantes ya tienen en mente.

units.source: "不用" ("no need to") says something isn't necessary, softer than 不要 ("don't") which sounds like a prohibition.

units.source: Using 不要 (don't, a prohibition) when you mean 不用 (no need to, simply unnecessary) - they carry different tones.
units.translation: Usar 不要 (no hagas, una prohibición) cuando se quiere decir 不用 (no hace falta, simplemente innecesario); tienen tonos distintos.

units.source: "都...了" ("all already") emphasizes that every item in a group has reached the same state - here, both vegetables are gone.
units.translation: "都...了" ("ya todo") enfatiza que cada elemento de un grupo llegó al mismo estado; aquí, ambas verduras se acabaron.

units.context: Scenario: Grocery Shopping & Meal Planning · Lesson: Making a Shopping List · grammar (Subject(s) + 都 + verb + 了)
units.source: Placing 都 after the verb instead of before it - 都 always comes right before the verb it's quantifying.
units.translation: Colocar 都 después del verbo en lugar de antes; 都 siempre va justo antes del verbo que cuantifica.

units.source: "还是...吧" ("I'll still go with...") signals a decision reached after considering alternatives - common when settling on a choice.
